name: Adani Ports & Special Economic Zone Ltd

debate.name: Adani Ports & Special Economic Zone Ltd

rounds.text: The intrinsic valuation suggests the market is under-estimating the company's worth, with a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 2432 per share compared to the market price of Rs 1761, providing a margin of safety of 27.6% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, a reverse discounted cash flow indicates that today's price implies only 13.6% earnings growth, which is well below the base case assumption of 18.0% [E47]. This growth outperformance is backed by historical strength, including a 5-year compounded profit growth of 21% [E19] and robust sales expansion that saw compounded growth of 25% over 5 years and 23% over 3 years and the trailing twelve months [E15, E16, E17]. Operational generation matches this expansion, highlighted by strong cash conversion of 1.59x in March 2026 where operating cash flow reached Rs 20,356 Cr and free cash flow stood at Rs 5,074 Cr [E34, E35, E36]. Institutional confidence is clearly building, shown by foreign institutions increasing their stake to 15.95% and domestic institutions raising theirs to 13.26% since December 2023, accompanied by a positive money flow signal [E42, E43, E44]. Conceded: the stock trades at a price-to-book ratio of 3.97x and a P/E of 29.2, sitting above sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6, E7, E61].

The valuation is stretched far beyond sector norms, with the stock trading at a price-to-earnings ratio of 30.97x against a sector benchmark of 17.56x and an elevated price-to-book ratio of 4.23x compared to a sector median of 1.38x [E6, E7]. This premium is further underscored by an EV/EBITDA multiple of 17.52x, which substantially exceeds the sector benchmark of 10.27x [E11]. Beneath these demanding multiples, leverage is expanding as borrowings climbed to Rs 65,998 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 63,566 Cr a year prior, while the current ratio of 1.39x provides only a thin buffer [E39, E38]. Operational execution also exhibits underlying volatility, as the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends both read inconsistent [E32, E33], and price growth has recently outpaced profit growth by 9%, signaling that market expectations are running ahead of fundamental delivery [E57]. Conceded: [E45], [E46].

Conceded: [E6, E7, E11, E32, E33]. While the bear highlights premium valuation multiples and inconsistent margin trends, these ratios overlook the company's superior operational returns and compound growth that justify market leadership [E8, E9, E10, E14, E15, E16]. The alleged pressure from expanding borrowings is offset by massive cash generation, evidenced by operating cash flow of Rs 20,356 Cr and a robust cash conversion ratio of 1.59x in March 2026 [E35, E34, E39]. Furthermore, the bear's concern regarding market expectations running ahead of fundamentals is neutralized by a valuation model showing a substantial 27.6% margin of safety and a reverse DCF proving that today's price requires an earnings growth rate lower than the historical baseline [E45, E46, E47]. Institutional confidence is firmly intact with positive money flows alongside increasing holdings from foreign and domestic institutions [E42, E43, E44].

Conceded: [E34, E35]. While cash conversion and operating cash flows are high, the bull glosses over the severe valuation expansion where the price-to-earnings of 30.97x, price-to-book of 4.23x, and EV/EBITDA of 17.52x all heavily outpace their respective sector benchmarks of 17.56x, 1.38x, and 10.27x [E6, E7, E11]. The bull cites historical compound growth and superior returns [E8, E9, E10, E14, E15, E16], but ignores that price growth has recently outpaced profit growth by 9%, signaling that expectations are already running ahead of delivery [E57]. Conceded: [E42, E43, E44]. Institutional holdings and money flows are positive, yet borrowings have simultaneously escalated to ₹ 65,998 Cr alongside a capital-work-in-progress build-up of ₹ 19,266 Cr that surged by 51.8%, exposing the company to significant project completion and leverage risks [E39, E40]. Furthermore, the bull leans on theoretical DCF safety margins [E45, E46, E47], but dismisses the company's historical vulnerability to extreme drawdowns reaching -80.2% paired with a high annualized volatility of 40.6% [E53, E54].
